messages:
jess (solutions): Hey team — customer reports a 400 from /v1/embeddings when sending a single item. They say it worked yesterday. Error: "Invalid input shape: expected a list of input vectors". Posting their payload and a curl repro. Can someone confirm if this is a server-side change or client encoding issue?

liam (support): can you paste the exact request body they sent + Content-Type header? usually 400 means the payload shape was wrong (single vec vs batch).

jess (solutions): sure, here is what the customer sent (node/axios):
```json
{
  "model": "text-embedding-embed-001",
  "input": [0.12, 0.03, 0.87, ...]  // single vector as a flat array
}
```
and their curl repro:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"text-embedding-embed-001","input":[0.12,0.03,0.87]}'
```

ara (eng): yep this will 400. Our embeddings endpoint expects `input` to be an array of input items (batch), so a single item must be wrapped as an inner array: "input": [[...]]. If you pass a single flat array the server treats each element as a separate input and then downstream vectorizer validates dims and fails. Server logs: `400 Bad Request - invalid input shape: expected list-of-vectors got vector-of-scalars (len=3)`.

sanjay (customer): oh wow — our internal helper was converting a single doc into its feature vector directly instead of wrapping it. Fixing now. Curious: why does the error mention dims? we send the right length (768) so should it have accepted it?

ara (eng): because the pipeline expects `input` to be a list-of-inputs. If you send one vector of length 768 as the top-level array, the service interprets it as N=768 inputs each of length 1. It then compares to the model's expected embedding dim (768) and fails: e.g. comparing (1) vs (768) -> mismatch. Error message could be clearer; filed internal task to make messaging explicit.

liam (support): short repro we used: correct payload:
```json
{
  "model": "text-embedding-embed-001",
  "input": [[0.12, 0.03, 0.87, ...]]
}
```
If using the SDK, `client.embeddings.create({model, input: [vec]})` — not `input: vec`

emily (product): noted — we should add a quick-warning in the docs and an example for single-item calls in both Python and JS. Also consider a helpful error: "expected input to be a list of items; for a single item send [[...]]".

jess (solutions): customer also reported a billing spike because they retried the call 10x while debugging. They sent a support invoice request for refund. liam — can you handle that?

liam (support): yes, I'll escalate billing. I already refunded the accidental spike for that API key.

ara (eng): quick note — we saw one edgecase where some client libs double-stringify the JSON and send `input` as a string (e.g., `"[0.12,0.03,...]"`). That also triggers shape errors and slower parsing causing slight latency spikes. If you see `Content-Type: application/json` but the server logs `invalid json in input`, check for double-encoding.

sanjay (customer): fixed the client, single-wrap did it. Thanks everyone. Appreciate the speedy turnaround and refund.

infra-bot: Incident logged: INC-2026-1003 — customer-embed-400-mis-shape. Severity: low. Assigned: eng/ara, support/liam.

liam (support): closing thread — doc task: add single-item example + explicit error text. Ticket: DOC-342.

jess (solutions): closing on our side. TL;DR: 400 due to shape (single vector vs batch). Fix: wrap single vector in an array or use SDK helper. Refund issued.
